chapter: Changing styles, the road and nightlife
title: From Dixieland to swing: stock arrangements and Ellington on radio
summary: He came in at the end of Dixieland and the start of swing, with stock arrangements until Ellington's radio broadcasts and Benny Goodman's Congress Hotel run.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Well, you talk about rock and roll, and earlier last week we were talking about bebop and swing and so forth. You 've seen and been through a lot of the musical changes in --
Yeah, right, right, right, right, right.
-- over the years. How do you view this?

Well, at the time, of course, when I first come into music, I was right on the end of Dixieland, the Dixieland craze, going into swing. And that's when guys like Archie Blyer and -- they used to write, Frank Skinner and guys like that used to write these arrangements, 'Business in F' and 'Business in Q' and all of that. That was just the beginning of the swing era.
Right, stock arrangements, and so they

didn't know too much about special arrangements until - and then guys like Duke started coming on the radio, and then they began to hear these real sounds, from the -- they called it the jungle band at that time. And then after that then all the other bands would come in on the radio and so this was the starting of the Swing era. And then this was before Benny, because Benny was --
Well, that was when Fletcher Henderson --
Right, right, right, Fletcher, right. Then Benny started, and when Benny started, this was about '33, I think, when he come into the Congress Hotel.
That was a little later then, maybe '35.
Was it? Was it '35? Right, right, right. And -- but all of that was the beginning of the swing, like I said. Then we went through the Swing era, and then we come into bebop, I guess it was.
